User benefit: Automatic log of reps and sets; removes manual entry; prerequisite for every other feature
What is actually measured: EMG burst events (E1-E3) and IMU segment motion; counts and timestamps
Evidence strength: IMU rep counting from wrist/forearm: ~91-93% of sets within ±1 rep (RecoFit; Soro 2019) [I, moderate]. EMG-burst counting from a belly-worn band: no validation found [H]
Hardware fit: Good. Both signals available; IMU on puck; works without a decision on sampling rate
Calibration: Per-exercise templates or thresholds; none per user expected
Expected limitations: Isometrics give no IMU motion; partials, pauses, rest-pause and co-contraction can split or merge bursts; static-segment exercises (curl for upper-arm band) rely on EMG and belly tilt, which is untested
Validation required: Stage 1 S1.6 on synthetic bursts; Stage 2/3 vs blinded video: ≥98% reps detected, ≤1 false rep per 50, on held-out users and each exercise [ENGINEERING TARGET]
Audit status / disagreements: A4 and A6 agree. A4/A6 disagree whether belly tilt helps counting on static-segment exercises: untested either way

User benefit: Descriptive log of how long a set lasted
What is actually measured: Time between first and last EMG burst (threshold-defined) and/or IMU motion duration
Evidence strength: Onset/offset detection works in lab gel EMG [I, moderate]; dry/textile bursts systematically longer than reference (Colyer 2018) [I, limited]; no outcome relevance - tempo 0.5-8 s/rep makes no hypertrophy difference (Schoenfeld 2015) [I, moderate]
Hardware fit: Good for set duration; burst onset/offset depends on noise floor and contact
Calibration: Rest baseline per wear for the onset threshold
Expected limitations: Thresholds shift with contact quality and sweat; not comparable across devices
Validation required: Onset/offset bias vs adjacent gel reference <50 ms and stable with contact quality [ENGINEERING TARGET]
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype as plain 'set duration' only; log burst-level electrical duration internally, do not display it as a metric
Audit status / disagreements: A4 originally: prototype as descriptive number. A6: log, don't display. A4 accepted (D15)

What is actually measured: Not tension. Electrical-activity duration or kinematic duration only
Evidence strength: No outcome evidence for any optimal TUT; repetition duration 0.5-8 s gives similar hypertrophy (Schoenfeld 2015; Lacerda 2021, n=10) [I, moderate]
Hardware fit: Cannot measure mechanical tension: no load, force or bar input
Expected limitations: A 'TUT score' invites slow reps with no demonstrated benefit; electrical activity continues in lockouts and is low in eccentrics
Validation required: None for a duration log; a TUT target cannot be validated because no target exists
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form. Show 'set duration'; drop the word 'tension'

Feature: Relative activation trend (EMG amplitude within a set)
User benefit: Shows the muscle's electrical activity rising as the set gets harder
What is actually measured: RMS amplitude per rep, relative to the first reps of the same set
Evidence strength: Amplitude rises across sets to failure in lab gel studies (Jenkins 2015; Sundstrup 2012) [I, moderate] but also rises with load, speed and effort, plateaus 3-5 reps before failure (Sundstrup 2012) and is limited by cancellation (Keenan 2005). Between-session amplitude CV ~41-43% even on reference systems (Colyer 2018). Dry studs: not validated [H]
Hardware fit: Measurable on one channel; sensitive to dry-contact impedance drift and band shift
Calibration: Within-set relative only; no cross-day comparison without a same-session reference contraction (Besomi 2020)
Expected limitations: Sweat lowers impedance over minutes and mimics an amplitude trend; band shift; load change resets it; users may chase a rising line
Validation required: Stage 3: within-set amplitude slope vs adjacent gel pair (CCC/LoA); show it is not explained by impedance or baseline-noise drift
Recommendation: Research-only / internal view until Stage 3 passes; never a user-facing score
Audit status / disagreements: A4 draft: prototype. A6: internal only (D1). A4 accepted. A3 adds: MDF is only safer than amplitude behind a signal-quality gate

Feature: Activation % ('is the target muscle doing the work')
Evidence strength: Requires MVC or standardised submaximal reference each wear (Burden 2010; Besomi 2020); amplitude ≠ force or tension (Vigotsky 2018); amplitude unrelated to anabolic signalling (Morton 2019) [I/M, moderate]
Hardware fit: One channel cannot apportion work between muscles; crosstalk at 25.4 mm IED unknown; orientation vs fibres unrecorded
Expected limitations: Crosstalk; fat thickness explains a large share of amplitude variance (Nordander 2003, trapezius); a percentage implies a known 100%
Validation required: Would need a defined construct first, then agreement vs reference with normalisation
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form

User benefit: Post-set description of how much the muscle's electrical signal showed peripheral fatigue
What is actually measured: Median/mean frequency per rep (phase-locked concentric windows), regressed across reps of one set
Evidence strength: Direction of spectral compression across sets to failure: [I, moderate] at group level in lab wired gel EMG (Jenkins 2015; Tsoukos 2021; Sakamoto 2012; Dimitrov 2006). Typical fall ~20-30% relative; no universal Hz values. At-failure MDF is load-dependent and the direction of load effect differs between studies (Tsoukos 2021 vs Yan 2025). MDF largely blind to type I fatigue (Gerdle 1992). On TENSR: [H]
Hardware fit: Requires DR ≥1 kSPS, preferably 2 kSPS: at 500 SPS sinc3 is -3 dB at 131 Hz and a true -25% drop reads ~-16% raw (verified datasheet; A3/A6 models). Orientation vs fibres unknown. Relative drop insensitive to 25.4 mm IED if aligned and stable
Calibration: Within one person, muscle, exercise and load; baseline reps of the same set
Expected limitations: Single-rep MDF SD ~9 Hz (0.5 s window) vs ~30 Hz total change: trend only reaches t≈2 near rep 8 of 10, so no live use. Joint angle and innervation-zone shift (up to 16 mm in biceps) move MDF; poor contact and mains hum bias it; not comparable across loads, days or users
Validation required: Stage 1 S1.3 at both data rates; Stage 2 S2-b slope reproducibility after re-application; Stage 3 slope agreement vs adjacent gel pair within 1.25× the two-reference-pair floor; Stage 4 must add predictive value over IMU-only and rep-count baselines or be dropped
Recommendation: Potentially useful after substantial validation - as a post-set descriptive trend only, gated by signal quality; never live, never a threshold
Audit status / disagreements: All agree on post-set only (C7, C17). A5 keeps a pre-registered research test of rep-level MDF against IMU baselines

User benefit: Would help users stop at an intended effort
What is actually measured: Nothing directly; a model over EMG + IMU features
Evidence strength: No dynamic free-weight sEMG RIR validation found; nearest is isometric biceps (Garofalo 2026, n=12) and an IMU+EMG RPE preprint where EMG added little [H, none]. Benchmark: lifter self-report has mean bias ~0.95 reps (SD ~1.45; Halperin 2022), MAE ~1.2-1.4 reps by our estimate; individualised bar-velocity models reach only <2 reps error (Jukic 2024)
Hardware fit: No load input, no bar sensor; spectral path needs ≥1-2 kSPS; IMU on limb segment
Calibration: Likely per user and per exercise (velocity precedent)
Expected limitations: Reps remaining depend on load, exercise and person; MDF slope arrives too late within a set; a biased cue pushes users past intended effort because feedback raises acute effort (Weakley 2023)
Validation required: Stage 4 R4.1: beat bias-corrected self-report in same sessions under leave-one-subject-out, upper CI of MAE difference <0; R4.2: beat IMU-only by ≥0.3 reps; R4.4: hold within RIR 0-3; S5.1 safety gate before any live use
Recommendation: Research-only. Never displayed as a number in v1

Feature: Set score ('did this set reach failure')
User benefit: Implied: confirms the set was hard enough
Evidence strength: No validation [H]. Outcome evidence: failure adds trivial or no hypertrophy over 0-3 RIR in trained lifters (Refalo 2023, 2024; Grgic 2022) and costs more fatigue; failure matters more at light loads (Lasevicius 2022; Robinson 2024 load moderation)
Hardware fit: Users already know if a rep stalled; IMU sees a stalled rep on moving-segment lifts
Expected limitations: Rep count and set duration separate failure from 3-RIR sets by construction (C18); rewards failure training the evidence does not support
Validation required: Only as a labelling check inside Stage 4 matched-rep analysis
Recommendation: Research-only; do not ship as a score
Audit status / disagreements: A4 draft: potentially useful after validation. A6: research-only (D2). A4 and A1 accepted. A1 nuance: a load-appropriate effort zone, not 'failure', would be the defensible target - but it depends on RIR, which is unvalidated. A4 would still log an IMU-detected stalled rep as user-confirmed metadata

Feature: Between-set recovery estimate / muscle-driven rest timer
User benefit: Implied: tells user when the muscle is ready
What is actually measured: Spectral recovery of a probe contraction, or of the next set's first reps
Evidence strength: Mills 1982: force half-recovered ~30 s, MPF ~3 min - spectral and performance recovery dissociate, and the direction differs across paradigms [I, limited]. No trial of EMG-guided rest. Outcome research already gives a default: >60-90 s, little gain beyond ~90 s for growth (Singer 2024); longer for strength (Schoenfeld 2016)
Hardware fit: A probe contraction adds work; resting muscle has no spectrum to read
Expected limitations: False precision; 'recovered' language implies readiness that is not measured
Validation required: Randomised within-subject trial: spectral-guided rest vs fixed 2-3 min on next-set reps at same load
Audit status / disagreements: A2 originally 'contradicted'; corrected to 'unvalidated' after Mills 1982 (C4). Recommendation unchanged

User benefit: Consistent rest; auto-starts at set end
Evidence strength: Defaults from outcome research: ≥90 s for hypertrophy, 2-3 min for heavy compound work (Singer 2024; Schoenfeld 2016) [I, limited-moderate]
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype, with no 'recovered' or 'ready' wording

What is actually measured: Would need two bands, one per side
Evidence strength: EMG asymmetry ≠ strength asymmetry; bilateral amplitude depends on placement, fat, impedance [I, limited]
Hardware fit: Not deliverable on one band: one channel per band. Two bands would need time sync (~10 ms), mirrored placement, per-side normalisation, matched electrode condition
Expected limitations: Placement differences dominate; 'imbalance' language edges toward injury claims (TGA)
Validation required: Two-band repeatability study with mirrored placement; agreement with dynamometry asymmetry
Recommendation: Research-only (and not available on current hardware)

Evidence strength: No validated definition of 'contraction quality' [H, none]. Strict vs momentum: similar growth in one untrained trial (Augustin 2025) [I, very limited]
Hardware fit: IMU could detect ROM shrinkage or momentum on moving-segment lifts only
Expected limitations: Rewards amplitude or a chosen tempo with no outcome basis; risk of encouraging squeezing or slowing with no benefit
Validation required: Define the construct first; narrow IMU ROM-shrinkage within a set is a later candidate
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading in its proposed form
Audit status / disagreements: All agree. Narrow IMU ROM-shrinkage on moving-segment lifts kept as a future hypothesis

What is actually measured: IMU segment rotation direction; EMG amplitude per phase
Evidence strength: IMU phase detection plausible where the worn segment moves [I, moderate]; no outcome reason to coach phase timing (Schoenfeld 2017c; tempo literature)
Hardware fit: Only when the instrumented segment moves (e.g. thigh band on squat; not upper-arm band on curl)
Validation required: Phase timing vs video/mocap per exercise
Recommendation: Potentially useful after substantial validation, restricted exercise list; log only
Audit status / disagreements: All agree; A4 keeps phase/ROM/velocity features restricted to moving-segment lifts

User benefit: Implied: tells user how much growth a set produced
Evidence strength: Contradicted: higher EMG did not mean more growth in the only direct test (Plotkin 2023, MRI); heavier loads raise EMG but give similar growth (Schoenfeld 2017a; Lopez 2021; Morton 2016); amplitude unrelated to anabolic signalling (Morton 2019); fatigue varies while growth does not across cluster/superset/drop-set/failure trials [I, moderate]
Expected limitations: Would be an invented number; encourages unnecessary fatigue
Validation required: Would require a longitudinal trial linking the score to measured growth within persons - not justified now
Recommendation: Unsupported or misleading - do not build
Audit status / disagreements: A4: unsupported. A6: contradicted. A4 adopted 'contradicted'

Feature: Weekly volume per instrumented muscle (set counts)
User benefit: Tracks the best-supported training dose variable
What is actually measured: Count of detected sets (and reps) on the muscle wearing the band, plus user tags
Evidence strength: Weekly sets per muscle is the best-supported dose metric, with diminishing returns (Schoenfeld 2017b; Pelland 2026) [I, moderate]
Hardware fit: One muscle per band; compound lifts feed other muscles fractionally (Pelland 2026)
Expected limitations: A 'hard set' filter needs RIR; un-instrumented muscles must come from exercise labels
Recommendation: Suitable to prototype as counts with user-tagged effort. 'Stimulus per muscle': do not build
